question: What is the primary goal of health education in nursing?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital drugs
options.C: Empowering people to manage their health
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital rules on patients

explanation: Health education equips individuals and communities with the knowledge and skills needed to take charge of their own well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why are nurse-patient interactions ideal for health education?

options.A: Hospital management requires daily teaching logs
options.B: Patients cannot read medical textbooks alone
options.C: Nurses have extra free time during shifts
options.D: Patients are vulnerable and receptive during illness

explanation: Healthcare encounters often happen during vulnerable moments, making patients more motivated to learn about recovery and prevention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which teaching principle involves avoiding heavy medical jargon?
explanation: Keeping language plain and using local terms ensures the patient truly understands the health instructions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: A nurse asks a diabetic patient to demonstrate how to check blood sugar. Which principle is applied here?
explanation: Having the patient physically demonstrate a skill engages them actively in the learning process instead of just listening. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the term for how adults learn differently than children?
explanation: Andragogy specifically refers to the methods and principles used in adult education, recognizing their unique learning needs. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does behaviourism apply to patient teaching?

options.A: Focusing only on what the patient reads in books
options.B: Using rewards or praise for good health habits
options.C: Explaining the deep anatomy of an organ
options.D: Giving long lectures without asking questions

explanation: Behaviourism relies on positive reinforcement, like praise or encouragement, to strengthen desired health behaviours. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which factor assesses if a patient is in too much pain to learn?
explanation: Physical readiness looks at bodily factors like pain, fatigue, or medication side effects that affect concentration. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: A newly diagnosed hypertensive patient is crying and refusing to speak. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report the patient immediately to the attending doctor
options.B: Teach family members instead while ignoring the patient
options.C: Hand out a detailed pamphlet on low-salt diets
options.D: Address emotional distress before attempting health teaching

explanation: High anxiety or shock impairs learning, so emotional readiness must be established before teaching can succeed. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the best teaching method for checking if a patient learned a physical skill?
explanation: Having the patient perform the skill back to the nurse ensures they actually mastered the physical technique. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: When is group teaching most effective in community nursing?

options.A: When dealing with a patient in severe acute pain
options.B: For administering emergency medications in the ward
options.C: For general public health topics like antenatal care
options.D: For teaching private wound care to an individual

explanation: Group teaching fosters shared learning and peer support for common community health topics. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the best approach when a patient has low reading literacy?

options.A: Giving them a longer medical textbook to read
options.B: Speaking very loudly in a formal medical tone
options.D: Using pictures, diagrams, and spoken explanations

explanation: Visual aids and verbal communication bypass reading difficulties and ensure the message is conveyed. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle a cultural health belief that conflicts with treatment?

options.A: Scold the patient for holding backward ideas
options.B: Respect the belief while calmly offering safe alternatives
options.C: Ignore the patient's culture completely during visits
options.D: Refuse to care for the patient until they comply

explanation: Respecting cultural context builds trust and opens the door for cooperative, safe health teaching. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which question best evaluates if a patient understood discharge instructions?

options.A: Do you understand everything I just said?
options.B: Can you tell me how you will take your drugs at home?
options.C: What will you eat for breakfast tomorrow?
options.D: Was this teaching session helpful for you?

explanation: Open-ended prompts require the patient to explain the instructions in their own words, revealing true comprehension. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why is documenting health education crucial in the patient record?

options.A: To prevent the doctor from ever talking to the patient
options.B: To satisfy hospital interior decoration rules
options.C: To ensure continuity of care across different shifts
options.D: To prove the nurse worked a full shift without rest

explanation: Accurate documentation lets other healthcare team members know what has already been taught to avoid repetition or gaps. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)

question: What role does a nurse play when speaking up for a patient's right to health information?
explanation: An advocate defends and protects the rights and best interests of the patient, including their right to understand their care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h8)

question: Why must a nurse collaborate with other health workers during patient education?

options.A: To avoid talking directly to the patient's family members
options.B: To ensure patients receive a consistent and unified message
options.C: To pass all administrative responsibilities to dietitians
options.D: To reduce the number of hours nurses spend in the hospital

explanation: Collaboration among doctors, nurses, and dietitians prevents conflicting advice and strengthens the patient's learning plan. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h8)
